sampling_rule.memory_row_definition: A memory row is emitted only when a concept is revisited within a sequence (first attempt on a concept produces no row). Features = [bias, log1p(attempts), success_rate, log1p(delta_steps), log1p(delta_days)].
sampling_rule.train_fit_rows: Iterate train.json in file order via memory_rows_by_sequence; keep first 200,000 rows; split by sequence id 80/20 (leakage_check=pass); fit logistic on the train-side sequences only.
sampling_rule.test_auc_and_confusion_rows: Iterate test.json in file order via memory_rows_by_sequence; keep first 80,000 rows. These exact rows produce the headline ~0.877 AUC and the confusion matrix.
sampling_rule.why_not_attempt_level_0_51: The ~0.51 figure is attempt-level correct rate on a 4k-sequence train sample (every attempt counts). The confusion matrix uses revisit-only memory rows from the first 80k test memory rows — a harder, non-iid slice with lower correct rate.

gap_explanation: Attempt-level train sample ≈0.51 includes first-time attempts. Memory rows are revisits only (train first-200k rate ≈0.479). The matrix/AUC slice is the first 80,000 test memory rows in file order (correct_rate=0.328), not a random sample of all test memory rows (uncapped test memory correct_rate=0.446). File-order capping over-represents harder early sequences → ~0.33 vs ~0.45.
